rationale: The title and abstract address methodological and socio-legal aspects of using Access to Information (ATI) and Freedom of Information (FOI) laws in Canada to obtain internal government records from policing, national security, and intelligence agencies. It has no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access (fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4; E01 wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the article is entirely off-topic (E01), focusing on Canadian Access to Information (ATI) / Freedom of Information (FOI) research regarding policing, national security, and intelligence records rather than water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: Getting at the Live Archive: On Access to Information Research in Canada
Individuals and organizations in Canada have a quasi-constitutional right to request information from federal, provincial, and municipal levels of government.
